text.p: Philippine oil refiner Petron Corp is expected to post a nine-month net profit of 3.18 billion pesos from the year-ago 1.979 billion pesos, a Reuter poll of six Manila brokerages on Friday showed.
Industry analysts said the rise could be attributed to projected revenues ranging from a low of 36.7 billion pesos to a high of 40 billion for the first three quarters of the year.
The start of the partial oil industry deregulation in June this year has yet to affect Petron, analysts said.
Petron, which is 40 percent owned by Saudi Arabia's Aramco, had last year shown a surge in profits in the fourth quarter, ending the year with a net income of 4.0 billion pesos.
Analysts said that kind of performance was unlikely this year and said profit growth in 1996 would be flat.

"I do not see any major improvement in both earnings and income. It's still a regulated industry despite the automatic oil price formula," Michael Gotera, senior analyst at Peregrine Securities (Phils) Inc, said.
The oil pricing formula allows oil firms to adjust prices monthly according to Singapore Posted Prices but the rise is limited to a maximum of 50 centavos per litre (1.9 cents).

The rest of the burden is passed on to a buffer fund called the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF) which has run a deficit and owes 1.24 billion pesos ($47 million) to oil firms of which Petron is meant to get 1.04 billion pesos ($40 million).
The analysts polled by Reuters said their profit projections included the expected receipts from the OPSF.
The start of deregulation was yet to help Petron as the government had still kept a lid on margins, Raul Ruiz, vice- president for research at Sun Hung Kai Securities, said.

Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities, projecting a nine month net of 3.217 billion pesos on turnover of 37.5 billion, said the pricing scheme's effect might only be felt towards end of the year.

"(But) next year will be very interesting for Petron when there will be free market competition. It will surely rise above its competitors because it has the highest return-on-rate base," said Alexis Cabel, analyst at Ang Ping & Associates.
It could lose a little to competition but it would still dominate the country's oil industry, analysts said of Petron which now controls 42 percent of the market.
Petron's results are expected in the third week of October.
Following are the 9-month profit forecasts:
(in billion pesos)
Ang Ping & Associates 3.247
CityTrust Investment Bank 3.18
DBS Securities Philippines Inc 3.4
Guoco Securities 3.217
Peregrine Securities 3.0
Sun Hung Kai Securities 3.05 to 3.1
